bib.title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

question: Which attention architectures (global vs local, which alignment functions, input feeding) work best for LSTM-based neural machine translation?
hypothesis: A local attention that looks at a window of source words can be cheaper and as good as or better than attending to all source words.
contributions: Global attention, a simplification of Bahdanau et al. (2015)
Local attention (local-m, local-p), a differentiable blend of hard and soft attention
Comparison of alignment functions (location, dot, general, concat)
New SOTA on WMT'14 and WMT'15 English-German; alignment quality evaluated by AER

method.summary: Stacking LSTM encoder-decoder NMT with a global or local attention layer (context vector c_t combined with h_t by a concatenation layer) plus optional input feeding. Trained on WMT'14 En-De and evaluated in both directions with ablations over alignment functions.

datasets.name: WMT'14 training data
datasets.size: 4.5M sentence pairs (116M English words, 110M German words)
datasets.split: pairs longer than 50 words filtered out
datasets.preprocessing: top 50K most frequent words per language as vocabulary; others mapped to <unk>; mini-batches shuffled

models.name: Stacking LSTM + attention (global/local-m/local-p)
models.context: sentences up to 50 words in training

training.objective: sum over (x,y) in D of -log p(y|x)
training.lr_schedule: after 5 epochs halve the learning rate every epoch (dropout models: start halving after 8 epochs)
training.seq_len: inferred: sentence pairs up to 50 words
training.dropout: used for LSTMs following Zaremba et al. 2015; rate not stated
training.regularisation: normalized gradient rescaled whenever its norm exceeds 5
training.hardware: single Tesla K40 GPU, ~1K target words per second

inference.samples: single run per system; ensemble of 8 models

parameters.AER decoding: force decode to reference, one-to-one alignment via max weight

metrics.name: BLEU (tokenized)
metrics.definition: case-sensitive BLEU with multi-bleu.perl after tokenizer.perl

metrics.name: AER
metrics.definition: alignment error rate vs RWTH gold alignments

baselines: WMT'14 winning phrase-based system (Buck et al., 2014)
eval.protocol: single training run per configuration; no significance test or seeds reported

availability.weights: models publicly available at same URL

results.quote: It takes 7–10 days to completely train a model.

limits: Concat alignment function underperformed and authors say more analysis is needed.
Not all architecture/alignment combinations run due to limited resources.
German-English did not match the WMT'15 SOTA phrase-based system.
AER and BLEU are not well correlated; alignment visualisations only in arXiv version.
Window size D, dropout rate and beam size not stated; single runs without seeds.
